'''Thanu Padmanabhan''' (10 March 1957 – 17 September 2021) was an Indian [[theoretical physicist]] and [[cosmologist]] whose research spanned a wide variety of topics in [[gravitation]], [[structure formation]] in the [[universe]] and [[quantum gravity]]. He published nearly 300 papers and reviews in international journals and ten books in these areas. He made several contributions related to the analysis and modelling of [[dark energy]] in the universe and the interpretation of gravity as an [[emergent phenomenon]]. He was a distinguished professor at the [[Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics]] (IUCAA) at [[Pune]], India.<ref>{{cite web |title=IUCAA - People |url=http://www.iucaa.in:8080/iucaa/jsp/N-People.jsp |website=IUCAA |access-date=8 September 2019 |archive-date=11 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111015055/http://www.iucaa.in:8080/iucaa/jsp/N-People.jsp |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Life and career==
Born to Thanu Iyer and Lakshmi on 10 March 1957 in [[Thiruvananthapuram]] (then Trivandrum), Padmanabhan attended school there. He earned his [[B.Sc.]] (1977) and [[M.Sc.]] (1979) in [[Physics]] from the [[University College Thiruvananthapuram]], part of [[Kerala University]].<ref name="Homepage of Padmanabhan" /> He published his first research paper (on [[general relativity]]) when he was still a B.Sc. student, at the age of 20.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF02846243 |title=T.Padmanabhan, Solutions of scalar and electromagnetic wave equations in the field of gravitational and electromagnetic waves, Pramana, (1977), 9, 371. |journal=Pramana |date=October 1977 |volume=9 |issue=4 |pages=371–384 |doi=10.1007/BF02846243 |access-date=2 December 2020 |archive-date=3 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180603150132/https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF02846243 |url-status=live |last1=Padmanabhan |first1=T. |s2cid=123557221 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>  He joined the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR) in [[Mumbai]] in 1979 for his [[Ph.D.]] and became a faculty member there in 1980.<ref name="Homepage of Padmanabhan" /> He held various faculty positions at TIFR from 1980 to 1992 and also spent a year (in 1986–87) at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]]. He moved to Pune to work at the [[Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics]] in 1992 and served as its Dean, Core Academic Programmes, for 18 years (1997–2015).<ref name=":0" />

Padmanabhan served as adjunct faculty of TIFR, the [[Harish-Chandra Research Institute]] ([[Allahabad]]), the [[Raman Research Institute]] ([[Bangalore]]) and the [[IISER|Indian Institute of Science, Education and Research]] (IISER, Pune) at different periods in his career. He was adjunct faculty of IISER, [[Mohali]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Prof. Padmanabhan: A Personal and Professional History|url=http://www.iucaa.in/~paddy/biodata/bio60.pdf|url-status=live|access-date=19 September 2021|archive-date=8 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008070415/http://www.iucaa.in/~paddy/biodata/bio60.pdf}}</ref>

Padmanabhan served as chairman (2006–09) of the Time Allocation Committee<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ncra.tifr.res.in/ncra/gmrt/gtac |title=GMRT Time Allocation Committee |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=2 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200202140143/http://www.ncra.tifr.res.in/ncra/gmrt/gtac |url-status=live }}</ref> of the Giant Meterwave Radio Telescope of NCRA. He was chairman (2008–11) of the Indian National Science Academy's National Committee<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/com.php |title=INSA |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=15 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115182700/http://www.insaindia.res.in/com.php |url-status=live }}</ref> which interfaces with the activities of the International Astronomical Union. In addition to advising the Government on policy issues, this also required him to coordinate the International Year of Astronomy 2009 activities in the country.<ref name=":1" />

He was elected president of the Cosmology Commission (2009–2012) of the [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) and provided advice to IAU activities in this field. He was elected in 2011 as chairman of the Astrophysics Commission (2011–2014) of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] (IUPAP)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://iupap.org/members-liaisons/ |title=Members & Liaisons &#124; IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=24 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200124093009/http://iupap.org/members-liaisons/ |url-status=live }}</ref> and co-ordinated the activities of IUPAP in this area. He was also a visiting faculty at many institutes including the [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Princeton University]], and a Sackler Distinguished Astronomer of the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]]. He was an elected fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] and of all three National Academies of Science in India (the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]).<ref name=":1" />

In addition to his scientific research, Padmanabhan worked actively to popularize science and gave over 300 popular science lectures and authored more than 100 popular science articles. He did a comic strip serial ''The Story of Physics''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scipop.iucaa.in/Literature/tsop/tsop01.html|title=The Story of Physics|access-date=17 September 2021|archive-date=17 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917194711/https://scipop.iucaa.in/Literature/tsop/tsop01.html|url-status=live}}</ref> aimed at school children. Published by Vigyan Prasar (New Delhi), it was translated into half a dozen regional Indian languages and made available at an affordable price at Indian schools. To commemorate the International Year of Astronomy (IYA) in 2009, he published (with [[Jayant Narlikar|J. V. Narlikar]] and Samir Dhurde) the IYA Astronomical Diary 2009,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iucaa.ernet.in/~scipop/Literature/iyadiary.html |title=IYA Diary: 2009 |website=www.iucaa.ernet.in |access-date=13 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121205014219/http://www.iucaa.ernet.in/~scipop/Literature/iyadiary.html |archive-date=5 December 2012 }}</ref> which comprises 53 illustrated pages of astronomical information. In 2019, he co-authored  with  Vasanthi Padmanabhan ''The Dawn of Science'' (published by Springer<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783030175085 |title=The Dawn of Science |year=2019 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-17509-2 |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=20 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120052412/https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783030175085 |url-status=live |last1=Padmanabhan |first1=Thanu |last2=Padmanabhan |first2=Vasanthi |isbn=978-3-030-17508-5 |s2cid=167177582 }}</ref>).

He was married to Vasanthi Padmanabhan, who has a Ph.D. in astrophysics from TIFR, Mumbai, and they had one daughter, Hamsa Padmanabhan, who herself has a Ph.D. in astrophysics from IUCAA, Pune.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Scientific community in Kerala mourns Thanu Padmanabhan's demise {{!}} Kochi News|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/scientific-community-in-kerala-mourns-thanu-padmanabhans-demise/articleshow/86312578.cms|url-status=live|access-date=19 September 2021|website=The Times of India|date=18 September 2021 |language=en|archive-date=19 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210919080340/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kochi/scientific-community-in-kerala-mourns-thanu-padmanabhans-demise/articleshow/86312578.cms}}</ref>

He died on 17 September 2021 at the age of 64 after a heart attack at his residence in Pune.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|date=17 September 2021|title=Renowned astrophysicist Thanu Padmanabhan passes away|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/renowned-astrophysicist-thanu-padmanabhan-passes-away/article36513555.ece|access-date=17 September 2021|issn=0971-751X|archive-date=8 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008070416/https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/renowned-astrophysicist-thanu-padmanabhan-passes-away/article36513555.ece|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=17 September 2021|title=Theoretical physicist Thanu Padmanabhan passes away in Pune|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/theoretical-physicist-thanu-padmanabhan-passes-away-in-pune-7514922/|access-date=17 September 2021|website=The Indian Express|language=en|archive-date=17 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917153742/https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/theoretical-physicist-thanu-padmanabhan-passes-away-in-pune-7514922/|url-status=live}}</ref> A tribute article written by his former graduate students and  post-doctoral fellows and physics friends from college days has been posted on the Physics arXiv.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Bagla|first1=Jasjeet Singh|last2=Bhattacharya|first2=Krishnakanta|last3=Chakraborty|first3=Sumanta|last4=Engineer|first4=Sunu|last5=Faraoni|first5=Valerio|last6=Kolekar|first6=Sanved|last7=Kothawala|first7=Dawood|last8=Lochan|first8=Kinjalk|last9=Modak|first9=Sujoy|last10=Nair|first10=V. Parameswaran|last11=Paranjape|first11=Aseem|date=2021-10-07|title=The Life and Science of Thanu Padmanabhan|class=physics.hist-ph|eprint=2110.03208}}</ref>

==Research==
Padmanabhan's research was on the fields of gravitation and cosmology which includes [[quantum gravity]] and nature of [[dark energy]].<ref name="Physics Reports 2003">{{cite journal |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0370157303001200 |last1=Padmanabhan |first1=T. |title=Cosmological constant—the weight of the vacuum |journal=Physics Reports |date=July 2003 |volume=380 |issue=5–6 |pages=235–320 |doi=10.1016/S0370-1573(03)00120-0 |arxiv=hep-th/0212290 |bibcode=2003PhR...380..235P |s2cid=119440437 |access-date=18 September 2021 |archive-date=27 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200527142325/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0370157303001200 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Padmanabhan |first=T. |date=January 2020 |title=Gravity and quantum theory: Domains of conflict and contact |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0218271820300013 |journal=International Journal of Modern Physics D |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=2030001–2030745 |doi=10.1142/S0218271820300013 |arxiv=1909.02015 |bibcode=2020IJMPD..2930001P |s2cid=202537535 |issn=0218-2718}}</ref> During 2002–2015, he provided a clear interpretation of [[gravity]] as an emergent phenomenon (like elasticity or fluid dynamics) and showed that this paradigm extends to a wide class of theories of gravitation including, but not limited to, general relativity.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1088/0034-4885/73/4/046901| title=Thermodynamical aspects of gravity: New insights| year=2010| last1=Padmanabhan| first1=T.| journal=Reports on Progress in Physics| volume=73| issue=4| article-number=046901| arxiv=0911.5004| bibcode=2010RPPh...73d6901P| s2cid=209835245}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1007/s10714-014-1673-7| title=General relativity from a thermodynamic perspective| year=2014| last1=Padmanabhan| first1=T.| journal=General Relativity and Gravitation| volume=46| issue=3| article-number=1673| arxiv=1312.3253| bibcode=2014GReGr..46.1673P| s2cid=119177380}}</ref> Padmanabhan could show that several peculiar aspects of classical gravitational theories find natural interpretations in this approach.<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1088/1742-6596/306/1/012001|title = Lessons from classical gravity about the quantum structure of spacetime|year = 2011|last1 = Padmanabhan|first1 = Thanu|journal = Journal of Physics: Conference Series|volume = 306|issue = 1|article-number = 012001|arxiv = 1012.4476|bibcode = 2011JPhCS.306a2001P|s2cid = 119249958}}</ref> Such an interpretation also provides a novel solution to the cosmological constant problem.<ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=1404.2284|last1= Padmanabhan|first1= T.|title= Cosmological Constant from the Emergent Gravity Perspective|journal= International Journal of Modern Physics D|volume= 23|issue= 6|pages= 1430011–1430458|last2= Padmanabhan|first2= Hamsa|year= 2014|doi= 10.1142/S0218271814300110|bibcode= 2014IJMPD..2330011P|s2cid= 119181469}}</ref> He gave two lectures at the Oxford–Cambridge collaborative conference on "Cosmology and the Constants of Nature" about this.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pcd911qSTBk |title=Video: Cosmological constants – Part 1 (Thanu Padmanabhan) |website=[[YouTube]] |date=4 June 2014 |access-date=27 January 2016 |archive-date=25 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200425140012/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pcd911qSTBk&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPkspt1XrKQ |title=Video: Cosmological constants – Part 2 (Thanu Padmanabhan) |website=[[YouTube]] |date=4 June 2014 |access-date=27 January 2016 |archive-date=23 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200423150450/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sPkspt1XrKQ&gl=US&hl=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

Popular (non-technical) descriptions of Padmanabhan's research have been published in [[Scientific American]] (India),<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140722003933/http://www.iucaa.ernet.in/~paddy/research/SAfinalarticle.pdf Article : ''Scientific American'' (India)]</ref> and a more technical description is available in an article from the [[Gravity Research Foundation]] in 2008, that describes his First Prize work. Another popular article about his work which appeared in a German science magazine<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vaas |first=Rüdiger |date=2014-11-18 |title=Die Atome der Raumzeit |url=https://www.wissenschaft.de/astronomie-physik/die-atome-der-raumzeit/ |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=wissenschaft.de |language=de}}</ref> along with the English translation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Atoms of Space-Time |url=http://www.iucaa.ernet.in/~paddy/research/german-article.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131081918/http://www.iucaa.ernet.in/~paddy/research/german-article.pdf |archive-date=2016-01-31 |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=iucaa.ernet.in}}</ref> An interview of Padmanabhan by George Musser about his work can be found [https://spookyactionbook.com/2015/12/23/an-interview-with-thanu-padmanabhan-video/ here].

In the earlier part of Padmanabhan's career (1980–2001), he made important contributions to [[quantum cosmology]], [[structure formation]] in the universe and statistical mechanics of gravitating systems.  In the 1980s, he came up with an interpretation of the [[Planck length]] as the 'zero-point length' of the [[spacetime]]  based on very general considerations.<ref name="AnnalsPhysics1985">{{cite journal |last1=Padmanabhan |first1=T. |title=Physical significance of planck length |journal=Annals of Physics |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S000349168580004X |date=November 1985 |volume=165 |issue=1 |pages=38–58 |doi=10.1016/S0003-4916(85)80004-X |bibcode=1985AnPhy.165...38P |access-date=18 September 2021 |archive-date=18 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918202751/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S000349168580004X |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref> This result, established by theoretical considerations and well-chosen thought experiments,<ref>{{Cite journal |doi = 10.1088/0264-9381/4/4/007|title = Limitations on the operational definition of spacetime events and quantum gravity|year = 1987|last1 = Padmanabhan|first1 = T.|journal = Classical and Quantum Gravity|volume = 4|issue = 4|pages = L107–L113|bibcode = 1987CQGra...4L.107P| s2cid=250887977 }}</ref> finds an echo in more recent results in several other candidate models for [[quantum gravity]]. He developed the complex path method (in 1998<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.60.024007| title=Particle production and complex path analysis| year=1999| last1=Srinivasan| first1=K.| last2=Padmanabhan| first2=T.| journal=Physical Review D| volume=60| issue=2| article-number=024007| arxiv=gr-qc/9812028| bibcode=1999PhRvD..60b4007S| s2cid=53450120}}</ref>) to study [[black hole thermodynamics]] which was a precursor to the 'tunneling paradigm' that became quite popular later on. He was a recognized authority in the subject of the statistical mechanics of gravitating systems<ref name="Physics Reports 1990">{{cite journal |last1=Padmanabhan |first1=T. |title=Statistical mechanics of gravitating systems |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370157390900513 |journal=Physics Reports |date=April 1990 |volume=188 |issue=5 |pages=285–362 |doi=10.1016/0370-1573(90)90051-3 |bibcode=1990PhR...188..285P |access-date=18 September 2021 |archive-date=8 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008070418/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0370157390900513 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref> and was a pioneer in the systematic application of these concepts to study the [[gravitational clustering]] in an [[expanding universe]].<ref>{{Cite book |doi = 10.1007/3-540-45835-2_7|chapter = Statistical Mechanics of Gravitating Systems in Static and Cosmological Backgrounds|title = Dynamics and Thermodynamics of Systems with Long-Range Interactions|series = Lecture Notes in Physics|year = 2002|last1 = Padmanabhan|first1 = Thanu|volume = 602|pages = 165–207|arxiv = astro-ph/0206131|isbn = 978-3-540-44315-5}}</ref> He was invited to lecture twice at the Les Houches Schools (in 2002 and 2008) to a broader community about this subject.

In November 2016, Padmanabhan published research studies advocating a new [[paradigm shift]] in understanding [[gravity]].<ref name="ARX-20161110">{{cite journal |last=Padmanabhan |first=Thanu |author-link=Thanu Padmanabhan |title=Do We really Understand the Cosmos? |arxiv=1611.03505 |year=2017 |doi=10.1016/j.crhy.2017.02.001 |volume=18 |issue=3–4 |journal=Comptes Rendus Physique |pages=275–291|bibcode=2017CRPhy..18..275P |s2cid=119214901 }}</ref><ref name="ENS-20161115">{{cite news |author=Staff |title=Research shows paradigm shift in understanding of gravity |url=http://epaper.indianexpress.com/c/14675133 |date=15 November 2016 |work=[[The Indian Express]] |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-date=20 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120010313/http://epaper.indianexpress.com/c/14675133 |url-status=live }}</ref> A key question in quantum gravity lies in understanding the primordial, pre-geometric phase of the universe, from which the classical, geometric phase described by Einstein's equations emerges along with the notions of space and time themselves. 
Padmanabhan introduced the notion of Cosmic Information (called 'CosmIn'), which allows these two phases to be connected in a fascinating manner. CosmIn, which is a [[conserved quantity]], measures the total information transferred from the quantum gravitational phase to the classical phase of the universe. Quantum gravitational considerations advocate an astonishingly simple value for CosmIn: 4π, the number of information 'bits' on the surface of a sphere of unit radius. Using these considerations, CosmIn was able to relate the numerical value of the [[cosmological constant]] – possibly the deepest unsolved problem in [[theoretical physics]] today – to the energy scale at which the universe made the quantum-to-classical transition.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269317306408 |title=Cosmic information, the cosmological constant and the amplitude of primordial perturbations |journal=Physics Letters B |date=10 October 2017 |volume=773 |pages=81–85 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2017.07.066 |bibcode=2017PhLB..773...81P |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=17 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917113228/https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269317306408?via%3Dihub |url-status=live |last1=Padmanabhan |first1=T. |last2=Padmanabhan |first2=Hamsa |arxiv=1703.06144 |s2cid=118886523 }}</ref> This is the first time that a model with no adjustable parameters is able to provide a holistic explanation for both these observations, which has far-reaching implications for the quantum structure of spacetime. A non-technical account covering this latest development in Padmanabhan's research was published in the magazine ''Nautilus''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://nautil.us/issue/53/monsters/the-universe-began-with-a-big-melt-not-a-big-bang |title=The Universe Began with a Big Melt, Not a Big Bang |date=5 October 2017 |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-date=21 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121134711/http://nautil.us/issue/53/monsters/the-universe-began-with-a-big-melt-not-a-big-bang |url-status=live }}</ref>

Padmanabhan authored several advanced level textbooks. In addition, he authored several popular-level science books.
